figures.alt: Empty commercial cold-storage room with insulated metal wall panels, sealed joints, refrigeration lines, and insulated doorway
figures.caption: Cold storage relies on a continuous insulated enclosure. Panel joints, penetrations, door openings, and the refrigeration layout must work together to control moisture movement and heat gain.
figures.before: The Physics Problem: Dew Point in a Florida Climate

figures.alt: Commercial cold-room ceiling with insulated panels, refrigeration evaporator unit, supported lines, and vapor-tight transition
figures.caption: Wall and ceiling panel systems need sealed transitions around refrigeration equipment and services. The durable envelope is a coordinated assembly, not insulation added after the mechanical work.
figures.before: Wall Panel Systems for Florida Cold Storage

figures.alt: Insulated cold-storage door threshold with sealed panel base, protective curb detail, and smooth floor transition
figures.caption: Floor and doorway transitions are part of the insulated enclosure. A coordinated threshold, panel base, and durable floor detail helps protect the cold-room boundary during daily operations.
